message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the last common ancestor of the two orders that contain them—Carnivora (the lion’s order) and Perissodactyla (the zebra’s order).  
Both orders belong to the super‑clade **Laurasiatheria**, so the common ancestor would have been a small, insectivorous mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, after the split of Laurasiatheria from other placental mammals. This ancestor is far older than the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (which dates back ~100–120 million years).
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The common ancestor of lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) would be a common ancestor in the mammalian lineage. Both are mammals, but lions are felids (family Felidae), zebras are equids (family Equidae). They diverged from a common ancestor in the order Carnivora vs Perissodactyla? Actually lions are in order Carnivora, suborder Feliformia. Zebras are in order Perissodactyla (odd-toed ungulates). So their common ancestor would be a more distant mammalian ancestor, perhaps the last common ancestor of placental mammals (Eutheria). But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species: that would be the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That would be the last common ancestor of the superorders Laurasiatheria? Actually Carnivora and Perissodactyla are both part of Laurasiatheria. So the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla would be the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria. That ancestor would be a small mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago. So answer: the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatheria, a small, insectivorous mammal that lived ~70-80 million years ago. Or we can say: the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and the order Perissodactyla, which is a small, early mammal from the late Cretaceous or Paleocene. Alternatively, we can mention the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which is older (~100-120 million years ago). But the more precise answer: the last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatheria, a small, insectivorous mammal that lived about 70-80 million years ago.
